title: VTA WebVH DIDs Keys Revoke — payload
description: Revoke a did:webvh key for compromise: withdraw it from its role in one entry, without overlap, record the compromise time so verifiers judge its past signatures accordingly, and put a generated replacement in its place where the role would otherwise be empty.

role.description: The role of the compromised key.

verificationMethod.description: The compromised key's verification method. REQUIRED for every role but `update`, and forbidden for `update`.

compromisedSince.description: The compromise time (VTI-KEY-121): the earliest instant from which the key is to be treated as compromised. Err early. Where it cannot be established, give the time the key was first published — `keys/list` reports it. MUST NOT be later than the request's `issuedAt`.

replacement.description: Generate a replacement in the same role, in the same entry. Absent means: replace only if the role would otherwise have no active key, with the revoked key's algorithm. Not permitted for `update`, whose replacement is the committed successor.

expectedVersionId.description: Optimistic-concurrency precondition: the versionId the caller based this change on (for example `keys/list`'s `versionId`). The VTA MUST refuse the change with `vta/webvh/dids:versionConflict` if the DID's latest entry no longer matches.

dryRun.description: Compute and return the preview without writing anything but the plan (CONVENTIONS.md §3.1). Absent reads as false.

previewId.description: Apply exactly the plan a previous dry run of this same request returned. The VTA MUST apply that plan or nothing, and MUST refuse with `vta/webvh/dids:previewStale` if it has expired, the log has moved past its base, or this request differs from the one previewed. An approval (step-up or quorum) is bound to this identifier.

reason.description: Why the change is being made, for the audit trail and for other approvers. Never published.

Response.title: VTA WebVH DIDs Keys Revoke — response payload
Response.description: Success response. Type https://trusttasks.org/spec/vta/webvh/dids/keys/revoke/1.0#response. A refusal is a `trust-task-error` document, never this.

preview.description: Present when `outcome` is `preview` or `pendingApproval`: the plan, and what an approval is bound to.

newVersionId.description: Present when `outcome` is `applied`: the versionId of the appended entry. Pass it as the next change's `expectedVersionId`.

keys.description: Every key whose state this change sets or would set, after the change.

serverless.description: True when no hosting server holds this DID. The caller must publish `newLogEntry` itself; until it does, resolvers still see the previous version.

newLogEntry.description: The appended entry as JSON text. Present when `serverless` is true.

followUp.description: What the node must now do that this entry cannot (VTI-KEY-133). Custody data, present for an `attestation` revocation.

statusListsToResign.description: Status lists signed by the revoked key, which the node MUST re-sign at once under a sound attestation key.

artefactsToReissue.description: Attestation artefacts still in force that the VTA's signing record shows the revoked key signed, which the node MUST re-issue.
